new.headline: You already have the endurance for a sub-3:45, so skip the 22-miler. This week drops a little and ends with your last long run on Sun Oct 4: 16 miles with 6 at goal pace.

answers.question: The race got moved two weeks earlier, to October 18, because of the bridge works. That's three weeks from today. I've only done one 20. Do I still have time for my 22-miler?
answers.answer:
No, skip the 22-miler. You already have the endurance it was meant to build.

- At your long-run pace of about 10:00/mi, 22 miles is roughly 3h40m on your feet. Beyond about 3 hours, a run wears you down more than it builds fitness.
- The only day left for it is Sun Oct 4, two weeks before the race. A run that long takes more than two weeks to absorb, so you would start the race still recovering.
- Your 20 on Sep 13 went well. You held a steady pace the whole way, and your heart rate rose only 7 bpm. With the 15 and 17 since then, your long-run work is done.

Instead, Sunday is 16 miles with 6 at goal pace near the end, and then the race taper starts. That run will do more for a sub-3:45 than six extra slow miles.

new.analysis:
**You ran last week exactly as planned.** All five runs matched their planned distances, and you took both rest days. Your threshold reps held 7:58/mi and slowed only 1 percent from first to last. That makes two weeks on plan in a row, after Sep 7 – 13, when you ran 53 miles against a planned 38.

**Your training shows you have the fitness for a sub-3:45.** Goal pace is 8:35/mi, and your threshold reps run about 35 seconds per mile faster than that. That gap is realistic but leaves little room, so run even splits on race day rather than banking time early.

| Run | Pace | Heart rate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Easy runs, Sep 22 – 26 | 9:52/mi | 138 average |
| Long run, Sep 27, 17 mi | 9:59/mi | 146 average, rising 5 bpm |
| Goal-pace miles, Sep 16 | about 8:35/mi | ending near 153 |
| Threshold reps, Sep 23 | 7:58/mi | peaking at 168 |

**With the race two weeks earlier, the taper starts now.** This week drops about 10 percent, to 38 miles, and the long run is a mile shorter. The hard work changes from building fitness to rehearsing goal pace, which is what the last weeks before a marathon are for.

**About 61 percent of your running time was easy (zones 1 and 2), and that is fine for a week like this.** The threshold session pushed time above zone 2. Your long runs also sit right at the top of zone 2, so part of each one counts as zone 3. Keep the easy days truly easy and that number will look after itself.

**The two weeks after this one get lighter.** The week of Oct 5 – 11 should be about 30 miles, with a 12-mile long run that includes a few goal-pace miles. Race week keeps short easy runs and a few goal-pace miles early on, so you start fresh but sharp.

**Keep both strength sessions this week, but make them lighter.** Use exercises you already know, at lower weights, and skip strength on Saturday before the long run. In race week, do light mobility work only.
